brief.goal: a 10-15 s Short that makes students try the phone-in-another-room trick
success: a viewer can explain the trick to a friend after one watch

shapes.text: the title is too small and too generic
shapes.reply: hook is 1.4x larger (96 -> 132 px, wraps to 3 lines inside the safe area) and now reads 'Your phone is stealing your study hour.' (r2a) instead of the generic 'Most of us check our phone...'

shapes.text: Hook A: "Your phone is stealing your study hour."
Hook B: "One hour. Phone in the other room."
Hook C: "You checked your phone 3 times reading this."

options.title: Keep the viral cut
options.summary: the draft as built: pop-in hook, saturated purple/orange gradients, whooshes, word-highlight captions
options.tradeoffs: most scroll-stopping; but it reads as hype, which you asked to avoid, and looks like every productivity short
options.cost: 0 s now; ~10 s for a sheet
options.taste: energetic and polished, but generic: the style shouts louder than the idea

options.title: Calm restyle
options.summary: same words and timing, 'clean' style: deep navy/teal gradients, slide-up words, crossfades, softer captions
options.tradeoffs: matches calm and the study mood; a quieter hook may lose some viewers in the first second; I swap the project for calm.mgl.json
options.cost: 0 s now; ~10 s for a sheet
options.taste: restraint fits the message: a calm video about putting the phone away practises what it preaches

rounds.why: the second one feels calmer and closer to how studying actually feels

options.title: Stealing your study hour
options.tradeoffs: names the cost to the student directly; a little negative; 6 words fits 2 lines at 132 px
options.taste: speaks to the exam crammer in their own terms

options.title: One hour, other room
options.tradeoffs: gives the trick away in the first second (best for 'explain it after one watch'); less curiosity, so the captions repeat it
options.taste: blunt and quiet: the instruction is the hook

options.title: You checked it 3 times
options.tradeoffs: playful pattern interrupt, strongest scroll-stopper; a claim we can't prove, and the playful tone leans away from calm
options.taste: wry, makes the viewer the subject

rounds.why: Stealing your study hour fits; it keeps the calm feel and stays within budget

options.title: Golden hour
options.tradeoffs: clearly warm and bright amber; highest contrast for white text; risks reading 'energetic' rather than calm
options.cost: 0 s (colour swap), then a ~10 s sheet

options.title: Dusky rose
options.tradeoffs: softer, evening-at-a-desk warmth that keeps the calm; lower contrast, so captions lean on their shadow
options.cost: 0 s (colour swap), then a ~10 s sheet
options.taste: quiet and intimate, ties to 'so does your evening'

options.title: Warm words, cool colours
options.summary: keep navy; warm the copy: CTA 'Try it tonight' instead of 'Follow for more', softer music bed
options.tradeoffs: cheapest and keeps the look you liked; may not be the warmth you meant
options.taste: warmth from voice rather than palette

rounds.why: Golden hour fits; it keeps the calm feel and stays within budget

rounds.goal: check pacing, captions and sound on the sheet

options.title: Ship the pacing as is
options.tradeoffs: no more work; but the trick is split over two captions ('Put it in another' / 'room for one hour.') and 'back, and so' reads oddly, which hurts 'explain it after one watch'
options.taste: fine, but the key line never lands as one thought

options.title: Phrase captions + warm CTA
options.summary: 3 cues on phrase breaks: 'Put it in another room.' / 'For one hour.' / 'Your focus comes back. So does your evening.'; captions 64 -> 80 px; CTA 'Try it tonight'
options.tradeoffs: the instruction lands whole and bigger; loses the word-by-word bounce; same 11.5 s
options.cost: 0 s edit, ~1 s stills to check, then draft ~10-20 s
options.taste: each line is a complete sentence: calm, readable, and the CTA asks for the action, not a follow

options.title: Phrase captions + 1.5 s hold
options.summary: as the second, plus the instruction held 1.5 s longer (13 s total)
options.tradeoffs: most comprehension and breathing room; 13% longer render and a slower middle may lose a few viewers
options.taste: lets the one idea sit, like a pause in a conversation

rounds.why: Ship the pacing as is fits; it keeps the calm feel and stays within budget

rounds.goal: approve the draft for the final render

options.title: Final as is
options.summary: render the draft you saw at full size
options.tradeoffs: no more changes; captions stay split as in the sheet
options.taste: warm, calm and clean; the hook carries it

options.title: Fix caption breaks, then final
options.summary: re-break the captions into whole phrases first, check with 2 stills
options.tradeoffs: clearer instruction for 'explain it after one watch'; you have not seen it in motion, so a small risk vs the draft
options.taste: the line that matters reads as one sentence

rounds.why: Final as is fits; it keeps the calm feel and stays within budget

log.text: hey, can you make me a short about focus? something people actually watch

it's for students cramming for exams, about 16-22. I want them to try one thing: phone in another room for an hour. success = they could explain the trick to a friend after one watch. calm, not hype-y. 10-15 s. please don't burn more than ~5 CPU minutes

Happy to. I drafted a 11.5 s Short from your script (phone in another room for an hour). Before I render anything: 5 quick questions in the Brief (who it's for, the one takeaway, what success is, tone, length and CPU budget).

Thanks, that's clear: students 16-22, one action (phone in another room for an hour), calm, 10-15 s, 5 CPU min. My draft is 11.5 s but styled 'viral' (pop titles, whooshes, saturated colour), which fights 'calm, not hype'. I'll put 2 directions on the board as stills next.
going with Calm restyle. the first felt a bit like every other productivity short

Calm it is: I've switched the project to the calm restyle (the storyboard stills now show it). On your pin p1: I made the hook 1.4x larger (96 -> 132 px). 'Generic' is a taste call, so 3 hook lines are in round r2; pick one and I'll apply it.

Done: hook is bigger and reads 'Your phone is stealing your study hour.' (still s2 is updated). Next rung is a contact sheet of the whole video (~5-10 s CPU, we've used ~3 s of 5 min): it shows pacing, every caption, and QA. OK to go?
'Warmer' can mean a few things, so round r3 has 3 readings: golden hour, dusky rose, or warm words with the cool palette. Stills of A and B are on the board (cost so far ~5 s of 5 min).
Golden hour applied to the project. Next rung: a contact sheet of the whole 11.5 s (est. 5-10 s CPU) to check pacing, captions and sound before any video render.
ok, Ship the pacing as is

The sheet is on the board (i-sheet1): no QA issues, loudness -14 LUFS. My concern: the trick is split across two captions. Round r4 has 3 options; I'd lean to the second (phrase captions + 'Try it tonight'), same length, no extra CPU.

Draft is ready: http://127.0.0.1:43461/files/renders/draft-1.mp4 (540x960, 11.5 s; it cost 14 s CPU, est. was 11 s; I started it a step early, sorry: I meant to check the estimate). Round r5: final as is, or fix the caption breaks first?
